home.metaDescription: Recon compares company ledgers with the data tax and customs authorities hold, and lists every disagreement with the rule it was checked under. Early development, synthetic data only.

hero.title: Where your books and the authority's copy disagree.
hero.lead: Recon compares company ledgers with the data each tax and customs authority holds, and lists every disagreement with the rule it was checked under.
hero.note: Early development. Everything shown here runs on synthetic data only.

field.caption: Illustrative only. Synthetic records, not real data.
field.description: Illustration: two ledgers side by side, Books and Authority copy. Most rows match and are joined by a line. One row differs and is flagged as a mismatch under a cited rule.

gap.title: The books say one thing. The authority's copy may say another.
gap.lead: A company's ledger and the copy a tax or customs authority holds are kept apart. When they drift, the difference can stay unseen until a notice, an audit or a closing review brings it up, and by then the reason is hard to reconstruct.

erp.title: ERP ledger exports
erp.body: The company's side: invoices and ledger entries exported from its accounting or ERP system.

clearance.title: Authority-side status
clearance.body: The authority's side, for example the clearance status of an e-invoice in a system such as KSeF, e-Factura or SdI. Today this record type is read from synthetic batches only; nothing is connected to a real authority system.

returns.title: Return and customs data
returns.body: Filed returns and customs declarations, compared with the books. No check for these exists yet.

pipeline.title: From an export to something you can verify.
pipeline.lead: Four stages. Each one is marked with what exists today.

ingest.name: Ingest
ingest.body: Reads exports and authority-side data into immutable, hashed batches. Only the batch API exists today; the adapters for ERP and authority sources are planned.

normalise.name: Normalise
normalise.body: Maps every source to one canonical record shape, so the same rule can read both sides.

reconcile.name: Reconcile
reconcile.body: Applies cited rules to both sides and records every disagreement. Check C1, invoice against clearance status, runs on synthetic data.

evidence.name: Evidence
evidence.body: Findings go to an append-only, hash-chained ledger. The chain verifier and the timestamp-token verification code exist; evidence packs are planned.

anatomy.title: Anatomy of a finding.
anatomy.lead: Every finding has the same parts, so it can be read, challenged and reproduced. The one below is synthetic.
anatomy.cardNote: Synthetic data. No real company or authority.

values.summary: Invoice {invoice} is recorded in the books as issued. The authority-side copy holds a different clearance status for the same invoice.

reproducible.title: Check and severity
reproducible.body: Names the deterministic check that ran. The same inputs under the same rule-pack version give the same finding, and no model decides it.

neutral.title: Summary
neutral.body: States only that two sources disagree. Recon is not a tax adviser: what to do about a disagreement is for the company and its advisers.

cited.title: Cited rule
cited.body: Names the rule the comparison was made under. Rules are versioned data that cite their source, and a human compliance owner approves them.

evidence.title: Inputs
evidence.body: Points to the exact records by hash, so the finding can be traced back and checked against the tamper-evident ledger.

principles.title: What does not change.
principles.lead: Constraints the product is built around. Where one is a design decision and not yet something that runs, it says so.

determinism.title: Same inputs, same findings
determinism.body: A finding is a pure function of the input record hashes and the rule-pack version. Running it again reproduces it. No model decides a finding.

isolation.title: Every tenant isolated
isolation.body: Row-level security in both databases keeps one tenant's records out of another tenant's queries.

ledger.title: Append-only ledger
ledger.body: Events are hash-chained per tenant and cannot be updated or deleted. A verifier recomputes the chain.

privacy.title: No personal data in logs
privacy.body: Logs, traces and ledger payloads are to be kept free of personal data.

rules.title: Rules are cited data
rules.body: Dates, thresholds and rates live in versioned rule packs with a source reference, never in code. A human compliance owner approves each change.

residency.title: EU-only residency
residency.body: Tenant data is meant to stay with EU-based processors. This is a design decision; the hosting provider has not been chosen yet.

closing.title: See where the two copies disagree.
closing.body: Recon is in early development and runs on synthetic data today. Sign in to look at the current build, or read which checks exist and which are planned.
